full_judgment:
The Rule was issued at the instance of the defendant No.6 on the following terms:

"Let the records be called for and a Rule issue calling upon the opposite party No. 1 show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 14-3-1996 and 19-3-1996 respectively passed by Additional District Judge, Magura in Title Appeal No. 134 of 1991 dismissing the appeal and affirming those dated 15-6-1991 and 19-6-1991 respectively passed by in Title Suit No. 111 of 1989 decreeing the plaintiff suit should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper."

2. The plaint case, in short, is that the plaintiff instituted title suit No. 111 of 1989 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sripur, Magura for declaration of title and confirmation of possession. It is stated in the plaint that Lalit Mohan Chakrabarty was a owner of 1.13 acres of land appertaining to plots No. 1093/1250/1786 of khatian No. 1044 and Malancha Dasi got the same executing kabuliyat on 19-6-1946. Rent suit No. 1660 of 1952 was filed against Malancha for nonpayment of rent and the same was decreed. In execution of the said decree, the suit land was sold in auction. The father of the defendant Nos. 1-5 Kartik Chandra Biswas purchased the same in auction and got the possession through Court and annulled all the encumbrances by filing case No. 117 of 1953 under section 167 of the Bengal Tenancy Act. Thereafter, one Shudanya alias Shudhansu filed Title suit No. 137 of 1956 for setting aside the aforesaid auction but the same was dismissed. Kartik Chandra Biswas the auction purchaser granted patta in favour of Belayet Ali Sheikh and Earuddin of 1.13 acres of land in 1362 B.S. i.e. 2-3-1956.

3. The defendant No. 11 Earuddin resides in non-suit plot No. 1786 and the rest 20 decimals of land of plot No. 1786 and 3 decimals of land of plot No. 1250 purchased by defendant No. 13 and 14 which are not including in the suit schedule 8 decimals of land of plot No. 1093 has been acquired by WAPDA and in the said plot the plaintiff is in possession of 6 and 1/2 decimals of land. The plaintiff is in possession for more than 12 years and thus, acquired title by adverse possession. The defendants have no right, title and interest in the suit land but they have been threatening to dispossess the plaintiff from the suit land and if they show any paper, those would have been created collusively, hence the suit.

4. The defendant No.6 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint and stated inter alia that 8 decimals of land of suit plot No. 1093 out of 20 decimals, 5 decimals out of 32 decimals land of suit plot No. 1250, 10 decimals of land out of 60 decimals of land of suit plot No. 1786 and 7 decimals out of 44 decimals of non suit No. 116 and 7 decimals out of 41 decimals of land of non suit plot No. 117 belonged to Sudanya and, the father of the defendant No.6 purchased those lands by registered kabala dated 26-2-1953. 8 decimals of land out of plot No. 1093 acquired by WAPDA and the father of the defendant No.6 got compensation. The suit land has been correctly recorded in SA Khatian No. 1144. Kartik Chandra Biswas became owner by auction purchase in respect of 12 decimals of land of suit plot No. 1093 out of 21 decimals, 21 decimals out of 32 decimals of land of suit plot No. 1250 and 50 decimals out of 60 decimals of land of suit plot No. 1786 of the same was correctly recorded in SA Khatian No. 1143. Kartik Chandra Biswas sold land to Ataur Rahman by registered kabala deed 28-5-1969 and the father of the defendant No.6 being co- sharer filed preemption case in respect of the said kabala being Miscellaneous case No. 523 of 1970 which was allowed on contest. Said Ataur preferred Misc. Appeal No. 42 of 1975 and the said appeal was dismissed and preemption was confirmed.

5. Defendant No. 11 is the alleged co-patta holder of the plaintiff who filed Title Suit No. 115 of 1977 in the Court of Munsif, Magura which was transferred to the Court of Munsif, Sripur and renumbered as Title Suit No. 495 of 1983 claiming 21 decimals of land of suit plot No. 1093, 1250 and 1786 covering by registered patta dated 3-3-1956 and in that suit the present plaintiff was proforma defendant No.3 and that suit was dismissed. The plaintiff and the present defendant No. 11 being dissatisfied with the judgment filed Title Appeal No. 67 of 1984 in the Court of District Judge, Magura and the appeal was dismissed. After being filed in that suit, the defendant No. 11 got the present suit instituted by the present plaintiff. The alleged patta dated 3-3-1956 as executed by Kartik Chandra Biswas is void as Kartik had no title at that time plaintiff had or has no cause of auction for-the suit which is liable to be dismissed.

6. At the Trial the plaintiff examined 3 PWs. And the defendant No.6 examined 4 DWs. To prove their respective cases.

7. The Trial Court upon considering the evidence on record and hearing the parties decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 15-6-1991 and 19-6-1991 respectively.

8. Defendant No.6 being dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree preferred Title Appeal No. 134 of 1991 in the Court of District Judge, Magura and the appeal on transfer was heard by the Additional District Judge, Magura who dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court.

9. The defendant No.6 again being dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court has preferred this revisional application before this Court and obtained the present Rule as stated above.

10. Mr. AH Mahfoozur Rahman learned Advocate along with Mr. Mashiul Alam, Advocate appearing. on behalf of the defendant No.6 petitioner has taken me through the judgment of both the Courts and placed the evidence of both the parties and submitted that the Trial Court on both facts and law committed error of law in passing the impugned judgment discarding the Rule of evidence. The evidence of DWs 2, 3 and 4 were also misread by the Courts below and further failed to note that the plaintiff filed the suit for declaration of title and confirmation and possession over only 52 and 1/2 decimals of land but the plaintiff produced PWs. 2 and 3 to corroborate the evidence of PW.l but PW.2 and 3 being the witness of possession only prove the possession of 16 decimals of land out of the 32 decimals of land of plot 1250 and without noticing, such evidence on record decreed the suit covering entire 52 and 1/2 decimals on surmises and, as such, the judgment of the Trial Court is not a judgment at all and that the Appellate Court without adverting to those materials on record affirmed the judgment of the Trial Court without having regard to the Order 41, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and thereby, both the Courts committed error of law in decreeing the suit which is an error in the decision occasioning failure or justice. The learned Advocate submitted Kartik Chandra Biswas admittedly the auction purchaser allegedly granted patta in favour of plaintiff arid the proforma defendant No.11 Earuddin by alleged registered patta dated. 3-3-1956 but in fact, Kartik Chandra Biswas had no superior interest over the suit land at the relevant time, on tlie operation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act stated on 13-12- 1955 at the locality and, as such, the.alleged patta is a void document. He further submitted tlre plaintiff has filed the suit only for declaration of title and confirmation possession without partition, as according to the plaintiff got the patta along with the proforma defendant No. 11 and, as such, the suit itself is not maintainable but this vital aspect of the case lost sight of the Courts below and decreeing the suit committed error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He submitted further that the plaintiff only produced patta which has been marked as Exhibit 1 and no paper showing act of possession has been produced before the Court but the plaintiff has filed the suit and examined himself as PW 1 and 2 other witness PW 2 and 3 to support his possession, but those 2 witnesses only corroborated to the extent of 16 decimals of land and even such, materials on record the Courts below finding the title and possession of the plain- tiff oven the entire suit land had decreed the suit and thus committed error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

11. The learned Advocate further submitted that the father of the defendant No.6 he had not purchased the land from Kartik Chandra Biswas and he had no onus to prove the title of Kartik, but Kartik Chandra Biswas sold his land to one Ataur Rahman by registered kabala dated 28-5-1969 and the father of the defendant No.6 being co-sharer filed the pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the preemption was confirmed up to Appellate Court, but said Ataur Rahman did not move the higher Court against the judgment, passed by the Appellate Court. The father of the defendant No. 6 got possession pursuant to the order of the Court passed in preemption case and in spite of such materials on record the Trial Court Shifted the onus to the defendant No.6 to prove the case as to title of Kartik which was not at all necessary because the father of the defendant No.6 only being preemptor got the land by pre-emption sold to Ataur Rahman by Kartik and in this score also the Trial Court as well as the Appellate Court have committed error of law in not noticing such evidence on record and decreeing the suit committed error of law resulting, in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate submitted further that the father of the defendant No.6 after receiving the judgment, and order of preemption case got mutated his name in SA Khatian No. 1144 and paid the rents and all the documents were made exhibits being exhibit No. Ka, Kha, Ga series Gha, Uma, Cha etc but those exhibits were not at all considered by the Trial Court as well as Appellate Court but decreed the suit which is liable to be set aside as committed error of law which has occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate has also submitted that the name of Kartik Chandra Biswas was recorded in SA Khatian which has been marked exhibit Uma(1) to show that Kartik had title and possession over the suit land who transferred his interest to Ataur Rahman and defendant father being co-sharer filed the pre-emption case and got the pre-emption but this aspect of the case was not taken into consideration by the Courts below and having passed the impugned judgment committed error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

12. In support of his contention the learned Advocate has referred to the section 17 sub section 3 of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act:-

"(3) A notification in the official Gazette of an order under sub-section (1) shall be conclusive evidence that the order has been duly made."

Notes

The Notification referred to in sub-section (3) of this section which has been published is Notification No. 18636 dated 13-12-55.

He has referred to the decision in the case of the Province of East Pakistan vs Muhammad Hossain Mia reported in 16 DLR (SC) 667 wherein their Lordships held:

"On the other hand, section 75 A, which was incorporated in 1954, came into operation only when a notification giving notice of the intention to undertake the preparation of the record of rights under section 17 (3) or of the compensation assessment roll under section 31 (1) had been given and it placed a complete embargo only on the subletting of any land in the khas possession of any rent-receiver within the area or areas specified in the notification and subletting, if made in contravention of the said section, was made null and void. The land so sublet was also to stand forfeited to the Provincial Government after the amendments made to the said section in 1956. The intention of this section appears to be that since after the acquisition of the interests of rent-receivers, rent-receivers were themselves to retain certain classes of retainable Khas lands as tenants directly under the Government, they should not be allowed to create further sub-tenancies under them. This was in keeping with the scheme of the acquisition Act, which was that after the acquisition of all rent-receiving interest anyone who held land within the province of East Pakistan should hold it as a tenant or raiyat directly under the government and not under anyone else as an intermediary.

'Sub-letting' has, of course, not been defined under the Act but under section 2 (31) of the Act words used in the first IV Parts of the Act (within which section 75A occurs) and not defined therein are to be given the same meaning as they bear in the Bengal Tenancy Act. Or Sylhet tenancy Act "Subletting" under the latter Acts connotes the creation of a subordinate tenancy or under raiyati under which the sub-lessee would but for a special contract be liable to pay rent for that land to a person other than the Provincial Government. Section 75A was intended to prevent this eventuality and this intention is made further manifest by the provisions of sub-section (3) thereof which provide that if any person holding land in his Khas possession does not wish to retain the same in his khas he may apply to the Provincial Government for the acquisition thereof on payment of compensation at the prescribed rate."

13. The learned Advocate then refers to section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and submitted that the alleged patta having been made in contravention of the sub section I of section 75A shall be null and void section 75A runs as follows:

"75A. Prohibition of subletting-(1) On and from the date of publication of a notification under sub-section (3) of section 17 or under sub-section (1) of section 31, no person shall sublet any land in his khas possession in the area to which such notification relates.

(2) Any subletting made in contravention of sub-section (1) shall be null and void and the land so sublet shall be forfeited to the Government.

(3) Any person may, at any time, apply to the Government for the acquisition of any of his khas lands under sub-section (2) of section 3 on payment of compensation at the rate prescribed for such land in section 39."

14. The learned Advocate submitted that the findings as to possession apparently arrived at by the Courts concurrently but those findings are contrary to law. But those findings are not findings in the eye of law. To support his contention he has cited the decision in the case of Khorshed Alam alias Shah A lam vs Amir Sultan Ali Haider reported in 38 DLR (AD) 133.

"28. All the Courts below in the facts and circumstances of the case had misplaced the onus on the defendant for proving the marriage of Monwara Begum with Amir Ali Mia where as the settled principle of law is that the person who deny it will have to be established in other words, it was for the plaintiff to prove that there was no marriage with Monowara Begum as alleged. As such, the concurrent finding of fact are no findings in the eye of law."

15. The learned Advocate. finally submitted that in framing of suit the plaintiff has not sought reiief against the SA Khatian No. 1143 appearing in the name of the Kartik Chandra Biswas, and so also against the order of preemption affirmed up to Appellate Court and, as such, mere declaration of title on the face of such documents are not at all maintainable but the Courts below on the face of such record have failed to notice those infirmity in the framing of suit and having decreed the suit both the Courts committed fundamental error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

16. On the other hand Mr Kazi Abdul Khaleque the learned Advocate along with Mr Mia Shirajul Islam Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff opposite party has refuted the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and submitted that Trial Court has very meticulously adverted to the evidence of the plaintiff as well as the defendant and decreed the suit and the Appellate Court affirmed the same having regard to the provision of Order 41, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure and findings being concurrent, these do not warrant interference in the revision. He then refers to the decision in the case of Md Shah A/am vs Farida Begum reported in 2 MLR (AD) 153 = 2 BLC (AD) 92.

"10. It appears from the impugned judgment that although the learned Judges have stated that the Courts below based their judgments upon misreading and non-consideration of the evidence, yet they failed to lay their hands on any part of the evidence of PWs and DWs or on any documentary evidence to bring home this error of law on the part of the Courts below. Without reversing the findings of the Courts below on the grounds mentioned in section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure the High Court Division has no-jurisdiction to disturb the final findings of facts. It cannot superimpose itself as a third Court for fresh appreciation of evidence. That is not its function in the revisional jurisdiction."

17. The learned Advocate submitted that the patta dated 3-3-1956 is a document of more than 30 years old and has been produced by the plaintiff as contemplated under section 90 of the evidence Act and which has got presumption of genuineness of the document and having regard to such evidence on record the Courts below decreed the suit and committed to error of law in decreeing the suit. The learned Advocate has referred the case of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) vs Md Reasuddin Pk reported in 5 BLC (AD) 76.

"10. An attempt has also been made to argue that the amalnama in question was wrongly accepted as evidence without any proof of its execution. The learned Counsel has, however, failed to satisfy us that the amalnama is not a 30 years old document and that it has not been produced from the proper custody. Once such a document more than 30 years old is produced from proper custody section 90 of the Evidence Act Entitled the Court to presume that it is a genuine document. The contention thus merits no consideration."

18. The learned Advocate further submitted the suit for declaration of title in the present form is maintainable in as such as real owner having been in possession is not required to file suit merely because his land has been wrongly recorded in the records of right and he can filed suit for declaration of title when any claim is raised on the basis of wrong recording of rights and has relied upon a decision in the case of Government of the Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner. Feni vs Har Chandra Nath reported in 10 MLR (AD) 313.

"10. The learned Additional Attorney-General submitted that the plaintiffs were very such aware of the preparation of the wrong record of right from 28-12-1970 when they obtained the certified copy of the Khatian recording the land in suit in the name of the Government. It may be mentioned the law is now settled that a real owner is not required to file the suit merely because his land has been wrongly recorded in the record of rights and he can very much wait until the person in whose name the record of right has been wrongly prepared raised claim in the land of the rightful owner."

19. The learned Advocate has submitted further that the plaintiff has also title by adverse possession and the Trial Court also found that the possession of the plaintiff and recorded findings that the plaintiff acquired the title by adverse possession and referred to the decision in the case of Nurjahan Begum vs Nur Rahman reported in 59 DLR 98, wherein a Division Bench of this Court held:

"30. The claim of the defendant No.1 as regard-schedule 'ka' and 'kha' that he acquired the same from his mother Maherunnessa by virtue of oral gift dated 15-12-1973 has not been substantiated. The learned Appellate Court in Appeal No. 25 of 1995 held that the oral gift dated 15-12-1973 has not been proved. The defendant No.1 also failed to prove the oral gift by the evidence of DW 5 who deposed that he did not see the mother of defendant No.1, Nur Rahman, and thus the fact of oral gift dated 15-12-1973 has not been proved. Both the Courts below also concurrently found that the oral gift dated 15-12-1973 has not been proved. Since the possession of the defendant No. 1 has been proved for more than 12 years, the defendant No. 1 is entitled to get title even on the basis of invalid title, though the defendant No. 1 did not specifically claim title by adverse possession vide the decision reported in 7 DLR 94."

20. The learned Advocate finally submitted that the plaintiff may be given an opportunity to seek appropriate remedy against the Khatian appearing in the name of Kartik and the orders passed in preemption case, remanding the suit to the Trial Court. The learned Advocate on the date of judgment has handed over Photostat copy DP Khatian 325/DP Khatian 859 and submitted that the name of the plaintiff has been recorded in the last khatian finding the plaintiff in possession and to that contention he refers to decision in the case of Erfan Ali vs Joynal Abedin Mia (late) represented by his legal heirs Golenur reported in 35 DLR (AD) 216.

"8. The rent-receipts were excluded from consideration by the lower Appellate Court taking the view that these are provisional receipts and that they carry little weight in that "any person interested in a land may pay rent to the Government Acquired Estate." This view is erroneous, for rent-receipts, though no documents of title are important items of evidence of possession any may be used as collateral evidence of title since possession generally follows title. Again plaintiff's name has also been recorded in the SA Khatian prepared in the period immediately following the whole-sale state acquisition in 1956 and all objections raised by defendant No. 1 were overruled by the Revenue-officer and then by the appellate authority. "

21. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff opposite party has also submitted that they are in possession by holding over as contemplated under section 116 of the Evidence Act and has relied upon a decision in the case of Khodeja Begum and another vs Sagarmal Agarwala alias Sombamal Agarwala reported in BCR 1987 (AD) 172, the relevant passage from paragraph 9 is re-produced :-

"Nevertheless, the lessee continued in possession with the consent of the landlords who realized rent from him after the expiry of the period of one year and in this way be continued till the Whole sale State Acquisition when he became a tenant directly under the Government. It is the possession of the lessee which is of fundamental importance in the case of holding over."

22. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has immediately stood up and raised objection to the submission of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff opposite party and submitted that the suit at this stage the suit cannot be remanded to the Trial Court after about 20 years of its filing in order to fill up the lacuna.

23. In view of submissions and counter submissions made by the learned Advocates and in view of the concurrent findings of facts concluded by the Courts below, I am called upon to consider the evidence of the parties.

PW 1 stated in chief

“১৭৮৬ নং দাগের পশ্চিম পার্শে ১০ শতাংশ জমিতে ১১নং বিবাদীর বসত বাড়ী এবং পূর্বের পার্শ্বে আমি বসবাস করিতেছি।”

“এবং ১০৯৩ দাগের ২১ শতাংশ জমির ৮ শতাংশ WPDA Acquire করিয়াছি। বক্রি ১৩ শতাংশের ৬.৫ শতাংশ আমি উত্তর পার্শ্বে দখল করি।”

PW 1 during cross examination stated.

XXX: আমি নালিশী জমির খাজনা দেই না কার্তিক চন্দ্র ১.১৩ শতাংশ নীলাম করে এবং আমাদের লিখিত বন্দোবস্ত প্রদান করে ১ম দখলের সাক্ষীনাই। নালিশী জমির খতিয়ান নং স্মরণ নাই। কার্তিক ব্যতিত অন্য কাহারো সাথে নালিশী জমির রেকর্ড হইয়াছে কিনা বলিতে পারি না।

PW 2 stated in chief

“আমি বাদী বিবাদী ও নালিশী ১টি দাগ চিনি। উক্ত দাগে ৩২ শতাংশ জমি; ১৬ শতাংশ জমি লইয়া মোকদ্দমা হইয়াছে। উহা বাদী দখল করে।

XXX: নালিশী দাগের বক্রি ১৬ শতাংশ জমি ১১ নং বিবাদী দখল করে।”

PW 3 stated in chief

“আমি বাদী বিবাদী ও নালিশী জমি চিনি। নালিশী ১টি দাগের জমি চিনি। উক্ত দাগে ৩২ শতাংশ জমি। ১৬ শতাংশ জমি লইয়া মোকদ্দমা। উহা বাদী দখল করে।

XXX: নালিশী জমির বেনালিশী ১৬ শতাংশ কে দখল করে বলিতে পারি না”।

Defendant has examined 4 DWs including himself as DW 1.

DW 1 stated in chief :

“WAPDA Acquire –ক্ষতি পূরণের টাকা আমার পিতা প্রাপ্ত হয়। নালিশী জমি আমি বর্গাদার যোগে দখল করি। আমি একজহন ডাক্তার; শ্রীপুর বাজারে আমার ফার্মেসী আছে। সত্য নয় যে, ১৩৯৬ সনের শ্রাবণ মাসের শেষ ভাগে আমি বাদীকে ভয় দেখাইয়াছি বা নালিশী জমি বাদী দখল করে।” ৪ খানা সরকারী খাজনার দাখিলা দাখিল করিয়াছি। প্রদর্শণী “গ” সিরিজ।”

“১১৪৩/১১৪৪ এসএ খতিয়ানের সহি মহুরী দাখিল করিয়াছি। প্রদর্শনী ‘ঙ’।”

“WAPDA কর্তৃক ৫ খানা নোটিশ দাখিল করিয়াছি। প্রদর্শনী ‘জ’ সিরিজ।”

XXX: বৈশাখ-জ্যৈষ্ঠ্য মাসে প্রথম দখলে গিয়াছিল। অদ্য হইতে ১৫-১৬ বছর আগে আমার পিতা দখলে গিয়াছিল। সত্য নহে, আমার পিতা নালিশী ভূমিতে কখনো দখলে যায় নাই।”

DW 2 stated in chief :

আমি বাদী বিবাদী, নালিশী জমি চিনি। নালিশী জমি আমি বর্গা চাষ করি। DW ৬নং বিবাদীকে ফসল প্রদান করি।

XXX: ৬০ শতাংশের দাগ নজরুল ১৪/১৫ বছর যাবৎ বর্গা চাষ করে। সত্য নয় যে, আত্মীয় বিধায় মিথ্যা সাক্ষ্য দিলাম।

PW 3 stated in chief :;

“আমি বাদী বিবাদী নালিশী জমি চিনি। নালিশী ৩২ শতাংশের দাগ আমি উড-১এর পক্ষে বর্গাচাষ করি।

XXX: সত্য নয় যে, আমার পুত্র DW-1 এর ঐষধ এর দোকানে থাকে বা আমি বর্গাদার নহি বা আমি পুত্রের খাতিরে সাক্ষি দিলাম।

PW 4 stated in chief :;

“আমি বাদী বিবাদী নালিশী জমি চিনি; নালিশী জমি আমি বর্গা চাষ করি; ৬০ শতাংশের দাগ DW-1 এর পক্ষে বর্গাচাষ করি।”

XXX: “সত্য নয় যে, আমি গ্রাম্য ডাক্তার বা আমি মাঠে যাই না।

The plaintiff instituted the suit for declaration and confirmation of possession with the prayer the relevant of which is quoted where under:

“বাদী পক্ষ করেন যে –

ক) আরজি বর্ণিত মতে ও কা��ণে নালিশী জমিতে বাদী পক্ষে সত্য দখল থাকা ও হওয়া মর্মে বিবাীদী পক্ষ বিরুদ্ধে সত্ব সাব্যস্থে পূর্বক দখল কায়েমের ডিক্রী দিতে।

খ) যাবতীয় আদালত ব্যয়ের ডিক্রী দিতে।”

The Trial Court after considering the evidence PWs recorded findings that:

“৬নং বিবাদী তাহার বক্তব্যের সমর্থনের ৪নং সাক্ষ্য প্রদান করেন এবং কতিপয় মোকদ্দমার আরজী ও আদেশের সহি মহুরী নকল ১টি খরিদা দলিল ২টি পর্চা, কতিপয় দাখিলা WAPDA কর্তৃক কতিপয় নোটিশ দাখিল করে যাহা যথাক্রমে প্রদ-ক, খ, গ, সিরিজ ঘ, ঙ, চ, ছ, সিরিজ হিসাবে চিহ্নিত হইয়াছে। DW1- ৬নং বিবাদী তাহার জবান বন্দীতে উল্লেখ করে যে, নালিশী জমি কার্তিক চন্দ্রের ছিল এবঙ নাঃ দাগের বেনালিশী অংশ সুধেন্দ্রের ছিল তাহার নিকট হইতে আমার পিতা কাজী বেলায়েত হোসেন খরিদ করে ২৬-২-১৯৫৬ ইং তারিখে”

then considered the evidence of DWs and came to the findings:

“বিবাদী পক্ষে বর্গাচাষ করে বলিয়া সাক্ষ্য প্রদান করেন কিন্তু জেরার কতিপয় প্রশ্নের উত্তরে বলে যে, DW1 আছমতউল্লাহর জামাতা মজিদ যে আমার ভগ্নিপতি ৬০ শতাংশের ধান আমি রোপন করি নাই ইত্যাদি‘ কাজেই এই পক্ষের সাক্ষ্য তেমন নির্ভরযোগ্য ও বিশ্বাস যোগ্য নয় বলিয়া মনে হয়; তৎপর DW3 স্বাক্ষ্য প্রদান করে যে ৩২ শতাংশের দাগে সে ৬নং বিবাদী পক্ষ বর্গাচাষ করে কিন্তু জেরায় এক প্রশ্নের উত্তরে বলে যে, “সত্য নয় যে আমার পুত্র এর ঔষধের দোকানে থাকে বা আমি বর্গাদার নহি কাজেই এই স্বাক্ষর বক্তব্যের সত্যতা অপর কোন সাক্ষ্য দ্বারা সমর্থন যোগ্য বলিয়া মনে হয়; বিবাদী পক্ষের ইত্যকার সাক্ষ্যে নাঃ ভূমিতে ৬নং বিবাদীর দখল আছে কিনা তাহা সুস্পস্ট নয় বলিয়া মনে হয়।”

24. It appears that the learned Assistant Judge disbelieved the DWs 2, 3 and 4 as they were related to the defendant No.1. Upon over all consideration finally came to the findings that:

“উহার বিরুদ্ধে বিবাদীর পিতা ৫২৩/৭০ নং মোকদ্দমা করিয়া ডিক্রী প্রাপ্ত হয় অতঃপর ১১ নং বিবাদী বাদীর কাগজপত্র লইয়া মোকদ্দমা করিয়া পরাজিত হয়; নাঃ ভূমি ৬নং বিবাদী দখল করে কিন্তু ১১ নং বিবাদী কর্তৃক দায়েরকৃত মোকদ্দমা রায়ের অনুলিপি প্রদঃ ‘খ’ দৃষ্টে দেখা যায় যে, উক্ত মোকদ্দমা সন্দেহাতীত ভাবে প্রমানিত না হওয়ারয় ডিসমিস করা হয় এবং উক্ত মোকদ্দমার আরজি দৃস্টে নাঃ ১০৯৩/১২৫০ এবং বেনালিশী ১৭.৮০ দাগের ১.৩০ শতাংশ ভূমি মধ্যে ২২.৭৫ শতাংশ ভূমি লইয়া মোকদ্দমা হয়িাছিল দৃষ্ট হয় কাজেই উক্ত ডিক্রির দ্বারা বাদীর নাঃ ভূমিতে স্বত্ব চলিয়া যায় নাই বলিয়া মনে হয়, ৬নঙ বিবাদী আরও দাবী করে যে ৫২৩/৭০ নং মোকদ্দমা মূলে এবং উহার আপীল ৪২/৭৫ নং মোকদ্দমা মুলে ও নাঃ ভূমি তাহার পিতা প্রাপ্ত হইয়াছিল কিন্তু উক্ত ৫২৩/৭০ নঙ মোকদ্দমায় রায়ের নকল প্রদ-১ক’ দৃস্টে নাঃ ভূমি উল্লেখিত দেখা যায় না এবং উহা একটি অগ্রক্রয়ের মোকদ্দমা দৃষ্টে হয় এবং উহার আপীল ৪২/৭৫ নং মোকদ্দমা ও নাঃ ভূমি উল্লেখিত দেখা যায় না তবে উহাতে নিম্ন আদালতের রায় বহাল রাখা হইয়াছে বিলয়া দৃষ্ট হয়, এবং উক্ত মোকদ্দমা বলে নাঃ ভূমিতে ৬নং বিবাদী দখল পাইয়াছিল বলিয়াও দৃষ্ট হয় না বিবাদী পক্ষের দাখিলী নাঃ ১১৪৪ নং খতিয়ানের পর্চা প্রদ-(ঙ) দৃষ্টে নাঃ ১৭৮৬ নং দাগে ৬০ শতাংশ ভূমি উল্লেখিত দেখা যায় এবং উক্ত ভূমি সহ উক্ত খতিয়ানের ২.০৩ শতাংশ ভূমি কার্তিক চন্দ্র বিশ্বাসের নামে রেকর্ডকৃত দেখা যায়।”

again came to the finding

“৬নং বিবাদী বাদীর বায়া কার্তিক চন্দ্র বিশ্বাস কর্তৃক জনৈক আতোয়ার রহমান বরাবরীয় ২৮-৫-৬৯ ইং তারিখের ১টি কবলা দলিল দাখিল করে উহাতে বাদীর কথিত নীলামের মোকদ্দমার কথা উল্লেখিত দেখা যায় এবং উক্ত কার্তিক চন্দ্র বাদীগণের দাখিলকৃত ৩-৩-৫৬ইং তারিখের পাট্টা দলিল জাল ঘোষণার দাবী করে নাই দৃষ্ট হয় কাজেই বাদী ৩-৩-৫৬ইং তারিখের পাট্টা দলিলের কৃত্রিমতা প্রমানিত হয় নাই বলিয়া মনে হয় এবং বাদীর উক্ত দলিল মুলে ও বিরুদ্ধ দখল জনিত স্বত্বে নাঃ ভূমিতে স্বত্বের উদ্ভব হইয়াছ বলিয়া মনে হয়, অবস্থা ধীনে নাঃ ভূমিতে ৬নং বিবাদীর স্বত্ব দখল আছে বা বাদীর স্বত্ব দখল নাই তাহা অনেকাংশেই প্রমানিত হয় নাই বলিয়া মনে হয় এবং অত্র বিচার্য্য বিষয় ৩টি বহুলাংশে বাদী পক্ষে প্রমানিত হইয়াছে বলিয়া মনে হয়।”

25. Upon analyses of the aforesaid evidence, pleading of the plaint along with the prayer and schedule and findings of the Trial Court, it appears that the Trial Court failed to notice that the plaintiff only submitted the patta deed 3-3-1956, exhibit-I and no papers showing his subsequent mode of possession has been produced before the Court. During the cross examination the PW 1 clearly stated that :“আমি নালিশী জমির খাজনা দেই না” and the name of the Kartik is still appearing in the khatians and such evidence clearly indicated that after the alleged patta the plaintiff did not take any step to record his land in the subsequent record of rights and admittedly, the plaintiff is not paying rent to the Government and no document had been produced .to show his possession in any manner in the suit land and the PW 2 and 3 only proved possession over 16 decimals of land out of 32 decimals of land in respect of plot No. 1250 but the plaintiff filed the suit for 52 and 1/2 decimals of land and thereby, it is clear that the plaintiff could not prove his title over the entire suit land as the PW 2 and 3 only allegedly corroborated to the extent of 16 decimals of plot No. 1250.

26. In view of the evidence on record, it is palpably clear that the plaintiff could not prove his possession over entire 52 II) decimals of land by any documentary or oral evidence and in this view of the matter, the findings of the Trial Court as well as Appellate Court appears based on total non consideration of the evidence on record and, as such, they committed serious error of law in not considering those aspect of the case and arriving at such conclusion and decreeing the suit. The defendant on the other hand submitted several documents which have been marked as exhibits from KaJha series. Exhibit 'ka' is the judgment and order passed in Misc. Case No. 523 of 1970 by which preemption was allowed, wherein the father of the defendant was the preemptor and on appeal the order of the Trial Court was affirmed (Annexure-Ka). It may be noted that Kartik sold his land vide exhibit-Cha(2) to Ataur Rahman by registered kabala deed dated 28-5-1969. The father of the preemptor being a co-sharer of the land instituted a preemption case No. 523 of 1970 in the Court of Munsif, 1st Court, at Magura and the pre-emption was allowed as aforesaid but no revision was preferred before the High Court Division and thereby, the judgment and order passed by the Trial Court as well as the Appellate Court remained, as such, and the defendant No.6 through his father having obtained possession pursuant to the order of the Court has been possessing the land and mutated his name, paid rents to the government and the defendants have filed those documents and marked as exhibits from Ga to Jha. On scrutiny of the judgment of the Trial Court, it has been found that the Trial Court has misconstrued the evidence and document as well as the orders of the competent Courts and upon such misinterpretation, misreading of evidence and records certain imaginary findings has been recorded and such findings, have been concurred by the Appellate Court. On perusal of the judgment of the Appellate Court, it appears that the Appellate Court mechanically affirmed the findings and decision of the Trial Court without adverting to the evidence to its proper perspective and upon, over all evaluation it further revels that the Courts below have committed gross illegalities in not considering the evidence to its proper perspective and thereby committed error of law resulting an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.

27. Now let me deal with the legal aspect of the case. The defendant petitioner acquired the title through preemption case as a co-sharer of the case land which was sold by Kartik to Ataur Rahman. It appears in the pleadings of the parties that Kartik admittedly acquired the land from Shudhamay and got the possession through Court and annulled all the encumbrances by filing case No. 117 of 1953 under section 167 of the Bengal Tenancy Act. Against the auction sale one Shudhanshu filed Suit No. 137 of 1956 for setting aside the aforesaid auction sale and the suit was dismissed and the sale was confirmed. Both the parties claim title through Kartik. The plaintiff allegedly took patta from Kartik on 3-3-1956 but thereafter, the plaintiff did not take any step to record his name in the relevant Khatian or mutated his name in the record and also admittedly has not paid rent to any authority, what so ever, since 1956. It is evident on record that the plaintiff has failed to show any papers showing possession except the patta and oral evidence of PW 1, 2 and 3. PWs 2 and 3 only allegedly proved possession over 16 decimals of land though the suit is for 52-1/2 decimals land. On the other hand the defendant claimed that after December 1955 the Kartik had no authority to grant patta holding rent receiving interest as rent receiving interest had already been ceased in view of publication of notification dated 13-12-1955 under sub-section 3 of section 17 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The defendant submitted that Kartik did not execute such patta as he had no superior interest. The plaintiff also did not take step to examine the signature of the Kartik in order to prove the patta. It has already been submitted that Kartik being owner recorded his name in the SA Khatians and being in possession sold land out of 3 plots vide exhibit-C to one Ataur Rahman and the father of the defendant No. 6 being co-sharer filed preemption case and got the preemption up to Appellate Court, but the plaintiff did never take any step to dislodge those SA Khatians as well as the sale deed executed by Kartik and so also the pre-emption case but remained silent. It appears further the defendant No. 11 who is the co-recipient of patta dated 3-3-1956 along with the plaintiff filed suit No. 115 of 1977 in the Court of Assistant Judge Magura and the defendant ultimately won the case in the Appellate stage contesting Title Appeal No. 485 of 1983 and on the face of such material evidence on record, the plaintiff did not take any step what so ever and such silence on the part of the plaintiff clearly proved that he failed to prove his patta deed and possession. It is on record that the defendant did not purchase land from Kartik but got the land of exhibit-'C' by preemption and, as such, from the evidence on record the defendant was not supposed to know about the basis of the acquisition of land by Kartik and, as such, defend in not bound to prove as to the acquisition of title by Kartik and in spite of such materials on record, Trial Court shifted the onus of proof upon the defendant and giving finding as such, it appears that the Courts below committed error of law. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff opposite party has tried to establish title on the basis of patta but no cogent evidence has been adduced before the Court. The learned Advocate has relied upon several decisions as noted above to get the decree on the basis of the decisions inasmuch as on the basis of holding over, adverse possession and as well as findings of the Courts below as the Courts below, concurrently settled the facts in favour of the plaintiff but the decisions cited by the learned Advocate are not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case.

28. The proforma defendant No. 11 appears to have allegedly got patta from Kartik along with the plaintiff but this defendant has not come to support the case of the plaintiff either as defendant or as witness but the plaintiff alone in support of the patta deposed but no one has been brought to support the patta and, as such, it appears that the patta has been left disproved.

29. As per section 17(3) the notification has been published vide notification No.18636 dated 13-12-1955 in the locality but the plaintiff has not produced any paper contrary to such evidence and, as such, it appears the patta allegedly granted by Kartik has been made in contravention of sub-section 3 of section 17 and the same was null and void.

30. The plaintiff filed the suit only for declaration but has not sought any declaration regarding the SA Khatian appearing in the name of Kartik, the kabala deed dated 28-5-1969 executed by Kartik in favour of Ataur Rahman and also against the pre-emption case filed by father of the defendant No.6 and has not sought partition making proforma defendant No. 11 Earuddin as principal defendant and, as such, in my opinion the suit as framed is not

maintainable in the present form.

31. The suit was filed in 1989 and by now about 20 years has been spent in the litigation involving the parties huge financial expenditure and, as such, I am not impressed on the submission of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite party to send the suit on remand to the Trial Court in order to afford opportunity to fill up the lacuna.

<u>32. I have already found that the Courts below have not adverted to the evidence on record to its true perspective and interpreted the evidence and given findings only on surmises. The trend of recording of findings by the Trial Court, it appears that the Trial Court has recorded findings and drawn conclusion without being sure as to purport of the evidence and documents. The appears on perusal of the judgment of the Appellate Court that the Appellate Court on cursory view has affirmed the findings of the Trial Court which has not fulfilled the object of Order  rule 31 of Code of Civil Procedure and thereby, it appears that both the Courts committed error of law in not considering the oral and documentary evidence to its proper and decision having not been passed in accordance with law should be interfered.</u>

33. In view of my above discussion made above, I find merit in this Rule.

34. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The judgment and decree passed by the Court below are set aside.

The suit is dismissed.

Send down the lower Courts records immediately.

End.

lawyer:
Rokanuddin Mahmud, Senior Advocate (with AM Aminuddin, Senior Advocate with Mustafizur Rahman Khan and Munshi Moniruzzaman, Advocates), instructed by Bivash Chandra Biswas, Advocate-on-Record—For the Appellant (In both the appeals). 
Mahbubey Alam, Attorney-General (with Murad Reza, Addl. AG and Israt Jahan, DAG and Mahfuza Begum, AAG) Instructed by Haridas Paul, Advocate-on-Record—For the Respondents. (In both the appeals).
parties:
British American Tobacco Bangladesh Company Ltd……….Appellant (In both the appeals)
Vs
National Board of Revenue, and others………Respondents (In both the appeals)
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 6-3-2016 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos.2848 of 2015 and 2849 of 2015).
full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J : Both these two civil appeals, by leave, are directed against the judgment and order dated 6-3-2016 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos. 2848 of 2015 and 2849 of 2015 making both the Rules Nisi absolute in part.

2. Facts leading to filing of these two Civil Appeals, in brief, are: That the appellant of both the appeals moved the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos. 2848 of 2015 and 284 9 of 2015, challenging two orders under নথি নং-৪/এলটিউ,মূসক/লিঃঅ্যাঃ/৯৭/বিএটিবি/দাবিনামা/২০১৪/১৪৮৭ both dated 22-3-2015 (Annexures-A and A(1) to both the writ petitions) both passed by writ-respondent No. 3 demanding Taka 7,98,24,23,593.01 as supplementary duty and VAT from the writ-petitioner for the period between financial year 2009-2010 upto 31st January of the financial year 2012-2013 and Taka 426,53,05,661.44 as supplementary duty and VAT for the period between 1st of February of the financial year 2012-2013 upto October of the financial year 2013-2014 claiming the same as violative of sections 5(2), 35, 36 and 55(1) of the VAT Act read with rules 3(3) and (7) of the VAT Rules and thereby obtained two Rules Nisi.

3. The appellant's cases in both the appeals being more or less similar, the sum and substance thereof is described below together to avoid unnecessary repetitions:— The appellant-company is a public company limited by shares and incorporated in Bangladesh. It carries on the business as a manufacturer and supplier of tobacco products including cigarettes. The appellant is the Bangladeshi subsidiary of the British American Tobacco Group/a multinational conglomerate headquartered in London, United King-dom. The brand-names of the appellant-company's manufactured products include amongst others BENSON & HEDGES, JOHN PLAYER GOLD LEAF, FALL MALL, CAPSTAN, STAR, SCISSORS, PILOT and BRISTOL. The appellant is enlisted with Dhaka and Chittagong Stock Exchanges. Its majority share-holder is the British American Tobacco Group holding approximately 72% of its issued shares. The appellant is registered with the VAT authorities (মূল্য সংযোজন কর কর্তৃপক্ষ) under section 15 of the VAT Act having VAT registration No. 5071005896 and it regularly pays VAT (মূল্য সংযোজন কর) and supplementary duty (সম্পূরক শুল্ক) on all its products i.e. cigarettes on the basis of retail price in terms of section 5(3) of the VAT Act on all of its products on the basis of price declarations submitted by it and as approved by the VAT authorities from time to time. The Government, by Gazette Notification No. এস, আর, ও নং-১৪৯/২০০১/৩১৪-মূসক dated 7tn June, 2001 (shortly stated as the notification), in exercise of its power conferred under section 14(1) of the VAT Act, exempted four classes of cigarettes from payment of supplementary duty (SD) at manufacturing stage in excess of various extents as mentioned in the said notification. Classification of all the manufactured cigarettes is done into four categories with reference to retail price brackets of the cigarettes. The notification had no reference for consideration of the quality, good will/reputation and /or brand value of the cigarettes. There is also no legal provision for classification of the cigarettes for exemption under section 14(1) of the VAT Act. The appellant, for its BRISTOL and PILOT Brand Cigarettes submitted price declarations on 19-8-2009, 9-11-2009, 12-8-2010, 23-6-2011, 27-6-2011, 21-6-2011 and on 25-6-2012 to the respondent No. 3, the Commissioner, Large Tax Payer's Unit (VAT) (hereinafter stated as the VAT Commissioner) under Rule 3, which were approved under Rule 3(3) of the VAT Rules within fifteen days firstly on 10-9-2009 and 30-11-2009. Thereafter, by General Order dated 23-12-2013 of the National Board of Revenue (NBR), all other price declarations were approved on 26-8-2010, 16-10-2010, 13-7-2011 and 2-7-2012. According to price declarations and approvals, the BRISTOL and PILOT Brand Cigarettes fell in the notification. The VAT authorities informed that it received complaints from local cigarette manufacturers that BRISTOL and PILOT Brand Cigarettes were, in fact, medium category cigarettes and the price being low it is causing huge loss to the national revenue although there was/is no scope under the VAT Act for testing the quality of the goods/cigarettes while approving the price declarations. NBR upon considering its aforesaid general order dated 23-12-2010 issued Memo dated 28-11-2012 clarifying the matter. But Respondent No. 4, the Additional Commissioner, Large Tax Payer's Unit (VAT) then submitted a report on 12-2-2013, reiterating the complaint. In the said report it was mentioned that due to increase of supply of BRISTOL and PILOT Brand Cigarettes of lower price category, huge deficit was caused in the revenue earning from cigarettes by 259.28% upto October, 2013 compared to the period upto October, 2012. The NBR thus collected samples of STAR, BRISTOL and PILOT Brand Cigarettes from the appellants' factory and sent the same to BCSIR for preparing a comparative statement of quality of BIRSTOL and PILOT Brand Cigarettes with STAR Brand Cigarettes, also manufactured by the appellant as a medium price category cigarettes. But no sample of cigarettes manufactured by local manufacturers was collected for comparative test or statement. Thereafter BCSIR sent chemical examination report dated 10-1-2013 to the respondents stating that PILOT, BRISTOL and STAR Brands Cigarettes were similar. On the basis of the said report respondent No. 4 by order dated 12-2-2013, calculated supplementary duty (SD) and VAT as ক্ষতিগ্রস্থ রাজস্ব  on account of BRISTOL and PILOT Brand Cigarettes for the period between January 2009-2010 to 2012-2013, 2009-2013 and February 2012-2013 to October 2103-2014 treating BRISTOL and PILOT Brand Cigarettes in the medium price category although the respondents admitted that the appellant submitted price declarations of BRISTOL and PILOT Brand Cigarettes and the VAT authorities approved the said price declarations which are also supported by the General Order dated 23-12-2010 and the appellants paid VAT and supplementary duty as per the said approved price declarations. Under such circumstances the appellant had /has no arrear VAT and SD to be paid, as there is not a single instance of (a) nonpayment of VAT by the appellant, (b) refund of VAT received by the appellant,

(C) drawback of VAT by the appellant and (d) adjustment being made by the appellant or any act as provided in section 37(2) of the VAT Act nor there is any mistake or incorrect explanation. It is thus claimed that though the appellant cannot be alleged to have committed an offence under section 37(2)(jha) of the VAT Act the VAT authority in exercise of power under rule 3(7) of the VAT Rules fixed the price of BRISTOL Brand Cigarettes as medium category cigarette. Pursuant to issuance of such order the appellant, ceased production, sale and supply of BRISTOL Brand cigarettes and side by side it also filed an appeal against the order dated 31-1-2013, which is pending before the Appellate Tribunal constituted under section 42 of the VAT Act.

4. It is further stated that the writ-petitioner recently came to know that by Memo No. নথি নং- ৫(১)/মূসক নীতি ও বাজেট/২০০৮/৪৬৬ dated 2-10-2013 the NBR, under the signature of respondent No. 7, sought an opinion from the Ministry of Law Justice and Parliamentary Affairs (shortly the Ministry of Law) as to whether it would be legal and justified to charge/realize VAT and supplementary retrospectively on the sale of BRISTOL Brand and PILOT Brand Cigarettes produced by the petitioner, on the basis of price applicable to medium price category cigarette. It is further stated that from the said Memo it is evident that though the NBR sought opinion from the Ministry of Law it made the demand without obtaining such legal opinion which the respondent No. 2 incorrectly stated that— 'the demand was made on the basis of advice of the Ministry of Law'. The respondent No. 3 vide Nothi No. 4 / LTU-Mushak / Ain /97/BATB/ Dahinama /13/9625 dated 24-11-2013 issued Demand Note upon the writ-petitioner-appellant for BRISTOL Brand Cigarettes under section 55(1) of the VAT Act demanding current register (Mushak-18) adjustment/payment of Taka 699,37,69,049.80 as "ক্ষতিগ্রস্থ রাজস্ব" (revenue loss) from the petitioner. Similarly vide Nothi No. 4 / LTU-Mushak /Ain /98 / BATB / Dabinama /13/9626 dated 24-11-2013 and vide Nothi No. 4/LTU-Mushak/ Ain/99/BATE/ Dabinama /13/9627 dated 24-11-2013 the respondent No. 3 demanded revenue loss of Taka 7,98,24,23,593.01 and Taka 4,26,53,05, 661.44 respectively against supplementary duty (SD) and VAT for PILOT Brand Cigarette for the period between 2009 to January 2013 and February 2012-2013 to October 2013-2014 under section 55(1) of the VAT Act. The appellant being aggrieved by the said two demand notices filed Writ Petition Nos. 12496 of 2013 and 12497 of 2013 before the High Court Division and obtained Rules Nisi with orders of stay. The Government of Bangladesh then filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal (CPLA) No.233 of 2014 and CPLA No.234 of 2014 before this Division, which were disposed of by two separate judgment and orders dated 7-4-2014 with direction upon the High Court Division to dispose of both the Rules Nisi upon staying the interim orders of stay granted by the High Court Division. Subsequently, the said two Rules Nisi were disposed of by the High Court Division vide judgment and order dated 21-5-2014 directing the writ respondent No. 3 to decide the matters under section 55(3) of the VAT Act considering the objection raised by the writ-petitioner-appellant. Meanwhile the appellant requested writ respondent No. 3 to withdraw the demand letters. In the meantime the Respondent No. 9 (Secretary Ministry of Law) opined that the provision of the VAT Act and the rules framed there under do not permit retrospective imposition and recovery of VAT and SD particularly when the price declarations of the appellant were duly approved by respondent Nos. 3 to 5 on year to year basis. Challenging the said opinion of respondent No. 9, one Dr. Md. Moshiur Rahman filed writ petition No. 2077 of 2013 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule and stay of the said opinion of the Ministry on 4-3-2015. Against the said order the present appellant filed Civil Miscellaneous Petition No. 214 of 2015 before this Division, which is pending. The present appellant also obtained Rule Nisi and stay order in Writ Petition No. 2773 of 2015 seeking direction upon the writ respondents not to dispose of the demand proceeding under section 55 of the VAT Act. Respondent No. 3 on 10-3-2015 heard the matter and issued letter on 12-3-2015 to the first Secretary NBR to appear and make submissions in favour of the VAT Authority. In view of the stay order passed in Writ Petition No. 2773 of 2015 the respondent No. 3 had no authority to pass the impugned adjudication/assessment orders under section 55(3) of the VAT Act in the matters. But the respondent No.3 without considering that VAT is an indirect tax and there is no provision for collection of VAT beyond the approved price and the petitioner having paid VAT and other taxes on the basis of approved price and on total misconception of section 55(1) and (3) of the VAT Act and rules 3(3) and (7) of the VAT Rules has arrived at an erroneous findings that the writ-petitioner-appellant has given false declarations violating the provision of section 5, 26(ka) 35, 36 and 55 of the VAT Act read with rules 3(3) and (7) of the VAT Rules and demanded payment of arrear VAT by the impugned orders. Hence, the writ-petitioner appellant filed the above noted writ petitions and obtained Rules Nisi.

5. Respondent No. 3 contested both the Rules Nisi by filing separate affidavits-in-opposition denying the allegations made in the writ petition and controverting the assertions made by the writ-petitioner-appellants. It is contended that subsequent to approval of price declared by the writ-petitioner appellants, it was found that the writ-petitioners made mis-declarations and also supplied untrue information in the declaration form, Mushak-1 and managed to get it approved. Upon detecting the same the Respondent No. 3, at his own motion, in exercise of power conferred by Rule 3(7) of the VAT Rules, held investigation and on the basis of test report acquired from BCSIR, found sufficient reason to re-fix the price of BRISTOL and PILOT Brand Cigarettes to upper segment of value base. The writ-petitioner appellant although questioned the property of such re-fixation, but he could not get any decision in his favour from any appellate/higher authority. The writ-petitioner appellant could not give any reason as to why it stopped production of BRISTOL Brand Cigarettes and, as such, it is apparent that the impugned orders passed by respondent No. 3 are lawful. The demand has been evolved due to evasion of VAT by way of mis-declaration of actual price. The price declarations were approved provisionally with condition “উল্লেখিত বিধিমালার বিধি-৩ এ বর্ণিত পরিস্থিতির আলোকে মূল্য সংযোজন কর কর্তৃপক্ষ কর্তৃক পরিচালিত কোনো তদন্তে বা জরিপে উপরিউক্ত ঘোষিত মূল্য ভিত্তি অসঙ্গতিপূর্ণ বা কম প্রতীয়মান হওয়ার ক্ষেত্রে উক্ত কর্তৃপক্ষ কর্তৃক নির্ধারিত মূল্য ভিত্তি অনুযায়ী ঘোষনা প্রদানের তারিখ হইতে কর প্রদানে আমি বাধ্য থাকিব।” set in Mushak-1 formulated under Rule 3 of the VAT Rules.

6. It is further stated that from the price approval letter dated 30-6-2013 it is evident that the concerned Divisional Officer approved the price subject to the condition “তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, যদি ভবিষ্যতে তদন্তে দাখিলকৃত মূল্য তথ্যে কোন অসংগতি বা অসত্য তথ্য পরিলক্ষিত হয় এবং এজন্য যদি কোনো সরকারী রাজস্ব প্রাপ্য হয় তাহলে গণপ্রজাতন্ত্রী বাংলাদেশ সরকারের অনুকূলে উক্ত পার্থক্যজনিত রাজস্ব জমা প্রদান করতে বাধ্য থাকবেন।” Thus it is stated that since the writ-petitioner appellant has supplied its product conceding the pre-condition as laid down in the approval order it is mandatory for it to deposit the sum found to be not paid in course of investigation/enquiry due to untrue/mis-declaration in respect of BRISTOL and PILOT Brand Cigarettes. It is further stated that from letter dated 10-9-2009 bearing Nathi No 4/LTU (Mushak)/25/ British/Tobacco/Mu: Anu:/Bibhag/Part-i/06/3791, it transpires that the representative of the writ-petitioner-appellant stated that BRISTOL and PILOT brand are not being marketed or sold in any other country of the world. Such statement is nothing but a gross misrepresentation inasmuch as these brands belong to principal of the writ-petitioner appellant company and are being marketed and sold by their principal's subsidiaries in rest of the world e.g. South America, Middle East, etc. Furthermore, these brands are being marketed and sold in India at a price of Rs. 47 which is the same rate that of CAPSTAN Brand Cigarette, a high segment cigarette of the petitioner company. Moreover, the Brands BRISTOL and PILOT are being sold in the international market at much higher price as evidenced in the pricing available in the online duty free shops. Thus on investigation since it has been found that the information provided in the submitted pricing information is not true and inconsistent the appellant is bound to pay the taxes for the difference. Moreover, pursuant to the directions passed in Writ Petition Nos. 12496 of 2013 and 12497 of 2013, the respondent No. 3 proceeded to determine the demand finally under section 55(3) of the VAT Act by applying judicial mind. The learned advocate's certificate issued in respect of Writ Petition No. 2773 of 2015 was received by respondent No. 3 after this respondent had already signed the note of the impugned orders at the early hours and dispatched the same on 19-3-2015 and 22-3-2015. Respondent No. 3 was not also in a position to consider the applications to adjourn the proceedings of adjudication in view of the directions passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos. 12496 of 2013 and 12497 of 2013. The VAT authority is empowered to demand VAT which has not been paid for any reason within a period of five years upon issuing demand notice under section 55(1) of the VAT Act. Thus the impugned adjudication/ assessment orders made under section 55(3) of the VAT Act has been rightly passed upon issuing the demand notice as per law.

Moreover, it is further stated that, the instant writ petitions are not maintainable inasmuch as the orders were passed by respondent No. 3 under section 55(3) of the VAT Act finally disposing of the proceeding and such orders being appealable under section 42 of the VAT Act and, as such, there being equally efficacious alternative remedy, the writ petitions are misconceived and not maintainable and, as such, the Rules are liable to be discharged.

7. The High Court Division upon hearing the parties and on perusal of the materials on record made both the Rules Nisi absolute in part by the impugned judgment and order dated 6-3-2016 holding that order under  নথি নং-৪/এলটিউ, মূসক/লিঃঅ্যঃ/৯৭/বিএটিবি/দাবিনামা/২০১৪/১৪৮৫ dated 22-3-2015 (Annexure-A to Writ Petition No. 2848 of 2015) and order under নথি নং-৪/এলটিউ, মূসক/লিঃঅ্যঃ/৯৯/বিএটিবি/দাবিনামা২০১৪/১৪৮৭ dated 22-3-2015 (Annexure- Al to Writ Petition No. 2849 of 2015) so far as it relates to financial year 2009-2010 only since the demand made by the respondents beyond the period of three years, issued by the writ respondents are declared to have been issued without lawful authority and of no legal effect. But rejected the prayer for declaring the demand order for the years 2010-2011 to 2013 to 2014 as illegal.

8. Being aggrieved by the said order of the High Court Division the writ-petitioner company as appellant preferred Civil Petitions for Leave to Appeal No. 1200 of 2016 and 1201 of 2016 before this Division so far it relates to the demand order for the financial year 2010-2011 to 2012-2013 and obtained leave giving rise to these two civil appeals. Interestingly the writ respondents, NBR did not prefer any appeal challenging the said order of the High Court Division so far as the Rules Nisi were made absolute in part.

9. Mr Rokanuddin Mahmud, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant in both the appeals submits that the High Court Division erred in law in not considering the fact that the earlier price declarations of the appellant for the said two brands of cigarettes at a lower category price having been approved by the VAT authority under rule 3(1), 3(2) and 3(3) of the VAT Rules, 1991, and there being no allegation from the VAT Authority that the appellants sold the said brands cigarettes at a higher price than the declared and approved one, there was no evasion of the VAT or supplementary duty by the appellants and hence the impugned demands were made without lawful authority and of no legal effect. He next submits that the examination conducted by BSCIR and the result of the appellants' cigarettes to the extent that the quality of the said two brands of cigarettes falls within the medium category price which would carry a higher rate of supplementary duty and VAT facilitating higher recovery of revenue which has now being claimed as lost revenue, is not at all acceptable because BSTI being the government authorized and approved authority to determine the standard of any product examination by BSCIR is not at all justifiable. Moreover, such finding of BSCIR was without any basis of law inasmuch as the classification of cigarettes under the VAT Act, 1991 and Rules framed thereunder has been made purely on the basis of the price declared by the company and approved by the authority at which the cigarettes were sold, not on the basis of its quality. Moreover, there was/is no provision in the VAT Act, or in the Rules, nor there was/is any relevant objective criteria, which would allow the VAT authority to examine and classify the cigarettes on the basis of its quality, basing upon which the manufacturer would be compelled to sell the cigarettes at a price falling under the medium price category rather than the lower price category at which the manufacturer submitted its price declaration, and got approval. In such view of the matter, the demands were entirely without jurisdiction, without lawful authority, and of no legal effect. He next submits that there was no scope under the law to make a retrospective demand of VAT and supplementary duty (SD) based on an enhanced rate other than on the price declarations that were previously submitted by the appellants and duly approved by the VAT authority, and hence the entire demand was without lawful authority and of no legal effect.

10. Mr Mahbubey Alam, the learned Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the respondents in both the appeals upon supporting the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division contends that the writ petition is not maintainable, as the writ-petitioner did not exhaust the available alternative efficacious remedy of preferring appeal under section 42 of the VAT Act, against any order passed by the Commissioner under section 55(3) of the said Act. He next submits that pursuant to section 55(1) of the VAT Act, the VAT authority has ample power to demand any VAT and/or supplementary duty (SD) evaded or not paid, for the reason whatsoever. In exercising such power the authority has to satisfy itself that such evasion or non-payment of VAT or SD is within five years. Accordingly, he submits that the demand being made within the period of five years from the date of evasion/non-payment of the same, within the stipulated time and in accordance with law, the impugned judgment does not suffer from any legal infirmity and, as such, this appeal should be dismissed. Mr. Alam further submits that the appellant company submitted untrue statement in their price declaration while obtaining approval but the same being conditional approval, the VAT authority has ample power to conduct investigation and upon holding such investigation the authority found evasion of VAT and supplementary duty (SD) by the appellant and, as such, it has rightly issued demand notice. Hence, no illegality has been committed in issuing the demand notice which has been categorically dealt with by the High Court Division while passing the impugned judgment and order. Thus he submits that the High Court Division rightly passed the impugned judgment and order on proper appreciation of fact and law for which both the appeals are liable to be dismissed.

11. Having heard the learned Counsel for both the parties and on perusal of the materials on record and the leave granting order it appears that three points have been raised in these two appeals for determination: (I) whether the High Court Division erred in law and facts in not considering that the earlier price declarations of the writ-petitioner appellant at a lower category price having been approved by the authority under rule 3(1), 3(2) and 3(3) of the VAT Rules, and there being allegation by the VAT authority that the writ-petitioner appellant sold the cigarettes at a price higher than that at which they were declared by the VAT authority, there was no evasion of VAT/supplementary duty (SD) by the appellant and hence the impugned demands were without lawful authority and of no legal effect; (ii) whether the High Court Division failed to consider and appreciate that the essential contention of the VAT authorities, which was that upon an examination of the cigarettes manufactured by the writ-petitioner it was found that their quality was such that they ought to have been declared at a medium category price carrying a higher rate of SD and VAT facilitating higher recovery of revenue, and which revenue was now being claimed as lost revenue, was without any basis in law inasmuch as the classification of cigarettes under the VAT Act, 1991 and Rules framed thereunder has been made purely on the basis of the price at which the cigarettes were sold, and there was no provision contained in the VAT Act, 1991 and the Rules framed thereunder, including any relevant objective criteria, which allowed the VAT authorities to examine and classify cigarettes on the basis of quality, and to further, based on such classification, compel the manufacturer to sell the cigarettes at a price falling under the medium price category rather than the lower price category at which the manufacturer submitted its price declaration, and in such view of the matter, the demands were entirely without jurisdiction and lawful authority, and of no legal effect and lastly (iii) whether the High Court Division failed to appreciate that there was no scope under the law to make a retrospective demand of VAT and supplementary duty (SD) based on an enhanced rate on the top of the price declarations that were previously submitted and duly approved, and hence the demand was without lawful authority and of no legal effect".

12. From the facts and circumstances as stated above and the questions raised in these two appeals it appears that it is required to see sections 5 and 7 of the VAT Act which deals with ascertainment of value for fixing VAT and also for imposition of supplementary duty (SD).

তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, বিভাগীয় কর্মকর্তা ঘোষিত মূল্য অপেক্ষা উচ্চতর মুল্যভিত্তি নিরূপণ করিলে সংশ্লিষ্ট নিবন্ধিত ব্যক্তি উক্তরুপ উচ্চতর মূল্য নিরুপণের তারিখ হইতে ত্রিশ কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে উক্ত নিরুপিত মূল্যভিত্তি পনুর্বিবেচনার নিমিত্ত কমিশনারের নিকট আবেদনের দাখিল করিতে পারিবেন এবং আবেদন প্রাপ্তির তারিখ হইতে পনের কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে কমিশনার উক্ত আবেদনের উপর সিদ্ধান্ত প্রদান করিতে ব্যর্থ হইলে তিনি আবেদনটি মঞ্জুর করিয়াছেন বলিয়া গণ্য হইবে ।

আরও শর্ত থাকে যে, স্বতঃপ্রবৃত্ত হইয়া বা বিভাগীয় কর্মকর্তা অনুরোধক্রমে মূল্যভিত্তি স্থির করার ক্ষেত্রে, কমিশনার কোনো পণ্য বা পণ্যশ্রেণির মূল্য বিষয়ে সুপারিশ প্রদানের জন্য, বোর্ড কর্তৃক আদেশ দ্বারা গঠিত, মৃল্যভিত্তিক পর্যালোচনা কমিটিকে অনুরোধ করিতে পারিবেন।

(৮) সরবরাহযোগ্য পণ্যের ঘোষিত মূল্য তালিকা পণ্য প্রস্তুতকরণ বা উৎপাদনস্থলের [বা ব্যবসায়স্থলে] এইরুপ কোনো

স্থানে আটিয়া রাখিতে হইবে যাহাতে উহা সহজেই দৃষ্টিগোচর হয়।

(৯) যে সকল উৎপাদিত বা সরবরাহযোগ্য পণ্যের ওপর আইন এর ধারা ৫ এর উপ-ধারা (৭) অনুযায়ী বোর্ড কর্তৃক

ট্যারিফ মূল্য নির্ধারণ করা হইয়াছে সে সকল প্রত্যেকটি পণ্যের জন্য নিবন্ধিত ব্যক্তিকে ফরম “মূসক-১ক” এ উপকরণ-উৎপাদ সম্পর্কে বা সহগ (input-output co-efficient) একটি ঘোষণা সংশ্লিষ্ট এলাকার বিভাগীয় কর্মকর্তার নিকট দাখিল

করিতে হইবে এবং বিভাগীয় কর্মকর্তা উক্ত ঘোষণাপত্র যাচাই বাছাই করিয়া প্রাপ্ত তথ্য প্রয়োজনে সংশোধনপূর্বক অনুমোদন

করিবেন এবং নিবন্ধিত ব্যক্তি উক্তরুপে অনুমোদিত উপকরণ-উৎপাদ সম্পর্ক বকা সহগের ভিত্তিতে ট্যারিফ মূল্যের অধীন পণ্যের প্রদয়ে মূল্য সংযোজন কর বা ক্ষেত্রমত, মূল্য সংযোজন কর ও সম্পূরক শুল্ক নিরূপণ ও প্রদান করিবেন।

তবে শর্ত থাকে যে, নিবন্ধিত ব্যক্তি কর্তৃক প্রদত্ত ঘোষণায় কোনো পরিবর্তন বা সংশোধনী আনয়নের ক্ষেত্রে নিবন্ধিত

ব্যক্তিকে যুক্তসঙ্গত শুনানির সুযোগ প্রদান করিতে হইবে ।”

<u>16. Having gone through the aforesaid provisions of law it appears that the present appellant was required, under section 5 read with Rule 3 of the VAT Act and Rules respectively, to submit their price list to the VAT authority for the purpose of approval of the same. The VAT authority, under Rule 3, is empowered to examine the price list submitted by the manufacturer and then either to approve or to reject the same upon classifying the goods within the time limit of 15 working days. Proviso to the said Rule 3 contemplates that “if no order is passed within 15 working days on the same either rejecting or approving, it would be deemed that the price list as submitted by the company/manufacturer is approved.” This clearly indicates that whatever step is required to be taken by the VAT authority viz examining classification, market price etc. that has to be done within that 15 working days time.</u>

<u>Subsequently, the VAT authority cannot, under any provision of law, claim VAT on the plea of wrong classification given in the price list.</u>

17. In the case in hand it appears that the price list of all kinds of products of the appellant company was sent to the VAT authority for approval and there was no allegation from any quarter, whatsoever, that they gave any false statement in the price list and the authority approved the same within the stipulated time of 15 working days without any objection. Nor was there any allegation that the appellant company sold the products at a higher price and thereby evaded payment of VAT as demanded by the VAT authority. It is to be noted that even subsequent to making such allegation of evading VAT on the basis of approved price list the VAT authority went on approving the same price list on ail subsequent years without raising any objection or determining that the classification of cigarette was wrong and the price ought to have been higher or lower than what has been proposed.

18. From the record it appears that on the basis of allegation of the local producer of the similar product the product of this appellant-company has been examined but none of the products of any such local company or even those of the complainant company has been examined or compared with the product of the appellant-company. Nor from the said order it appears that there is any indication that any such material has been produced, to indicate what is the nature of the complaint or under what authority such complaint was lodged by the local producers.

19. It is further to be noted that the product was examined in the Laboratory of BCSIR whereas the government run organization, BSTI is the appropriate authority to examine and compare the standard of any product. But in the present case, the government without relying upon their own approved authority for examination and comparison of the standard of the appellant-company's goods/products relied on the report prepared by BCSIR a separate organization. Thus the report of BCSIR always remains questionable.

20. In the instant case, the main allegation of the appellant is that the VAT authority on the basis of complaint lodged by the local producers compared the products of the appellant-company much later than the statutory time limit of 15 days for approval of the price list and without comparing the product of so called complainant and relying on non-government laboratory report alleged that the appellant's products were of such standard for which VAT and supplementary duty should have been imposed on a higher rate which is totally beyond the scope of law.

21. The High Court Division failed to take into consideration the aforesaid aspect that after approval of the price list by the VAT authority the appellant continued selling its products on the basis of the said approved price list and thus the authority acted beyond the scope of law specifically the 15 working days time limit and thereby imposed extra burden of payment the arrear VAT and SD, in the name of evading VAT and supplementary duty (SD), upon the appellant company. It is also admitted that even after lodging such complaint the authority went on approving the price list submitted by the appellant company. Thus it clearly shows that the authority did not act in accordance with law it blew hot and cold together which is not fair and justified in accordance with law.

<u>22. Another question has been raised as to the maintainability of the writ petition. In this respect, the High Court Division, as it appears from the impugned judgment and order, upon proper consideration of the materials on record came to the definite finding that the writ petition is maintainable. But the Government did not prefer any appeal against such finding or challenge the same. The finding of the High Court Division as to maintainability of the writ petition appears to be acceptable. Moreover, maintainability of writ petition is a mixed question of fact and law. And unless it is alleged and challenged, the same cannot be looked into when there is apparent violation of law causing infringement of both statutory as well as fundamental right.</u>

<u>23. In this respect, admittedly the National Board of Revenue (NBR) did not challenge the finding of the High Court Division in respect of maintainability of the writ petition thus now it cannot, under any circumstance, raise the question of maintainability of the writ petition.</u>

<u>24. Moreover, from the record it appears that after approving the price list the VAT authority informed that on the basis of complaint lodged by some local cigarette manufacturers they made the allegation that the writ-petitioner is evading payment of VAT and supplementary duty and also causing revenue loss to the Government. It also appears from the record that inquiries were held but the authority, without testing or comparing the goods of the alleged local cigarette manufacturers brought such allegation against the appellant and came to such conclusion that the appellant has evaded payment of VAT and supplementary duty and thereby caused revenue loss to the Government. This action of the VAT authority appears to be illogical as none of the products of the local cigarette manufacturers was compared with the products of the appellants and thereby making such omnibus allegation that they have evaded payment of VAT and supplementary duty. It further appears from the record that the VAT authority even after bringing the allegation of payment of VAT and supplementary duty at a lower rate in comparison to other manufacturers cigarette of similar brand the same price list which was submitted subsequent to making such allegation in respect of two brands of cigarette of the appellants, the VAT authority continued approving the same at the same rate which were sold earlier pursuant to the approval made by the VAT authority. And the VAT authority in violation of section 55 of the VAT Act demanded VAT and supplementary duty from the appellants upon amalgamating all the years irrespective of beyond four years of limitation and thereby made the impugned demands which was challenged in the above noted writ petition.</u>

<u>25. From the above facts and circumstances it is clear that the entire action of the VAT authority shows that the VAT authority dealt with the appellants in an arbitrary manner and with an intention to penalize the appellants without following the procedure of law. The appeal preferred before the appellate authority also shows that these aspects have not been considered even by the appellate authority. When the entire action of the VAT authority appears to be illegal, mala fide and arbitrary on the face of the record, invoking article 102 of the Constitution, under such circumstances, without preferring statutory appeal, is no bar. Thus we are view that the High Court Division correctly held that the writ petition was maintainable and accordingly disposed of the matter. But the disposal in respect of asking the appellant to pay VAT and supplementary duty for the period from February, 2012-2013 to October, 2013-2014 is not in accordance with law.</u>

<u>26. Thus it is clear that since there is violation of law and fundamental right of a citizen in charging VAT and supplementary duty (SD) giving retrospective effect beyond the provision of law and since there is violation in demanding such duty/tax it cannot be said that the writ petition was not maintainable.</u>

<u>27. Accordingly, we find substance in the submissions of the learned advocate for the appellants in both the civil appeals and the same are liable to be allowed.</u>

Hence these two civil appeals are allowed without any order as to costs.

End.
